title: Al-I'tisam
author: ash-shatibi
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: Al-Shatibi's study of innovation and adherence to the prophetic path: what counts as a religious innovation, how it differs from legitimate practice, and why the distinction matters for law and worship. It gathers scriptural evidence and the positions of earlier scholars, and closes with a defence of the middle way against both excess and neglect.
historicalContext: Written in Granada in the fourteenth century, when Sufi practice and legal reform were contested in al-Andalus. The I'tisam applies the author's theory of the purposes of the law to the question of religious practice and became a standard reference in later debates over bid'a.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
